title: Why does watered-down coffee give you more caffeine?

scenes.title: Watered-down coffee with MORE caffeine?
scenes.voice: Watered-down coffee with more caffeine? Sounds impossible, but there's a catch.

scenes.title: Concentration ≠ total
scenes.text: Espresso is more concentrated, but the big cup holds more caffeine in total.
scenes.voice: Espresso is more concentrated, but it's tiny. The big cup is more diluted, and it still packs more caffeine overall.

scenes.title: By the numbers
scenes.text: An espresso has about 63 mg. A cup of filter coffee, about 95 mg.
scenes.voice: A shot of espresso has about sixty-three milligrams of caffeine. A cup of filter coffee, about ninety-five.

scenes.title: Reason 1: extraction
scenes.text: More water and more contact time pull more caffeine out of the bean.
scenes.voice: Reason one: extraction. More water and more contact time pull more caffeine out of the grounds.

scenes.title: Reason 2: more coffee
scenes.text: A cup of filter coffee uses almost twice the ground coffee.
scenes.voice: Reason two: a cup of filter coffee uses almost twice as much ground coffee.

scenes.title: Careful with the Americano
scenes.text: Adding water to an espresso does NOT add caffeine: it just spreads it out.
scenes.voice: But careful: adding water to an espresso doesn't give you more caffeine. It just spreads it through more liquid.

scenes.text: What counts is the total caffeine you drink, not how strong it tastes.
scenes.voice: What wakes you up is the total caffeine you drink, not how strong it tastes.

scenes.text: Team espresso or team big mug?
scenes.voice: So, are you team espresso or team big mug? Follow for more.
